item.title: Priority Technology to go private in $1.6 billion CEO-led deal
item.description: Payments and banking solutions provider Priority Technology Holdings said on Monday it had agreed to be taken private by a group led by Chairman and CEO Thomas Priore in a deal valued at about $1.6 billion.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Payments and banking solutions provider Priority Technology Holdings (PRTH.O) said on Monday it had agreed to be taken private by a group led by Chairman and CEO Thomas Priore in a deal valued at about $1.6 billion. The group will pay $8.05 per share in cash for those it does not already own, representing a 65% premium to the stock's unaffected price before the initial proposal was disclosed in November 2025. The agreed price is more than 30% above Priore's initial offer of $6 to $6.15 per share. Funds advised by Searchlight Capital Partners have provided equity commitments for the acquisition. The transaction was unanimously recommended by a special committee of independent directors following a review conducted with its legal and financial advisers. The agreement includes a $15.75 million termination fee for Priority and a $35.25 million reverse-termination fee payable by the buyer. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027.

item.title: ＣＮＮなど3社、米政権提訴 ホワイトハウス排除は報道の自由「侵害」
item.description:
Susan Heavey
［ワシントン ２１日 ロイター］ - 米メディアのＣＮＮ、ＭＳ
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Susan Heavey

［ワシントン　２１日　ロイター］ - 米メディアのＣＮＮ、ＭＳ ＮＯＷ、ポリティコは２１日、所属記者のホワイトハウスへの立ち入りを禁止されたことについて、合衆国憲法修正第１条で保障された言論・報道の自由を侵害しているとして、トランプ政権を提訴した。

３社は、コロンビア特別区連邦地裁に訴訟を提起すると政府側に通知したと明らかにした。早ければ今週中にも緊急審理が開かれる可能性があるという。

３社は共同声明で「ホワイトハウスは事前の通知も手続きもなく、われわれの報道内容を問題視して記者証を取り消した。異議を申し立てなければ、報道の自由と、政府の介入を受けない独立した報道を受ける国民の権利が脅かされる」と説明。提訴は「憲法修正第１条で保障された権利を守り、政府が報道機関の報道・発行内容を決めるものではないという原則を擁護する」ことが目的だとした。

トランプ大統領は、３社による提訴の発表後、自身の交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）「トゥルース・ソーシャル」で改めて排除方針を擁護し、証拠を示すことなくメディアは安全保障上の脅威だと主張。「ホワイトハウスは、私が大切にしている『報道の自由』への攻撃を行っているのではなく、『フェイクニュース』への攻撃をしている」と投稿。「腐敗し、意図的で、広範囲に及び、完全に組織化されており、全く制御不能だ。これはわが国の国家安全保障に対する脅威であり、今すぐ止めなければならない！」と述べた。

トランプ氏は１８日に３社をホワイトハウスから排除する方針を表明し、他の報道機関も締め出す可能性を示唆。３社によると、所属記者らは１９日、ホワイトハウス敷地への立ち入りを拒まれ、記者証を没収された。

ＣＮＮは、３大ＴＶネットワークのＡＢＣ、ＣＢＳ、ＮＢＣ、ＦＯＸニュースと並び、ホワイトハウスの主要なＴＶ代表取材（プール取材）を構成し、撮影した映像を他の報道機関と共有している。

ＣＮＮは２１日にトランプ大統領が国連総会出席のためニューヨークを訪れる映像を提供する予定だったが、不可能となった。これを受け、他社もホワイトハウスの代表取材を停止し、事実上、ホワイトハウス関連イベントに関する重要な映像ソースが途絶えることになった。

ＦＯＸニュースのワシントン支局長は電子メールで、取材対象となっていたトランプ大統領関連のイベントの代表取材は２１日から行われないと発表。「ホワイトハウスがＣＮＮに対し、割り当てられた代表取材の義務を履行を妨げる立場を受けた措置」とし、「代替の代表取材は設置されない」と述べた。

item.title: 中国、軍制服組幹部2人の党籍剥奪 重大な規律・法律違反
item.description: ［北京 ２１日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［北京　２１日　ロイター］ - 中国共産党は２１日の政治局会議で、軍制服組トップだった張又俠・国家中央軍事委員会元副主席と劉振立・軍事委元委員の党籍剝奪を決定した。「重大な規律・法律違反」が理由。国営通信新華社が伝えた。

１月に両氏に対する調査が発表され、８月下旬に中央軍事委員会から解任された。

新華社は公式文書を引用し、両氏が「政治規律と政治ルールを著しく違反し、派閥を形成し、党に対して不忠実かつ不誠実であった」とした。

両氏が汚職により私腹を肥やしたとし、「関与した金額は極めて巨額であり、（行為の）性質は極めて深刻で、その影響も極めて甚大であった」と指摘した。

item.title: Erosion of Germany's political centre exposes Merz's weakening grip on power
item.description: The AfD also recorded its best-ever result in Berlin, where the far-left Left Party came first and looks set to replace Merz's conservative Christian Democrats (CDU) in the mayor's office.
item.dc:creator: James Mackenzie
item.content:encoded: Germany's far right and far left both made big gains in Sunday's [USN:L1N45C01D TEXT:"state elections"], exposing yet again the erosion of the political centre in Europe's largest economy as well as Chancellor Friedrich Merz's weakening hold on power. The anti-immigration Alternative for Germany (AfD) confirmed its strength in the formerly communist eastern states by taking first place in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania state, building on its [USN:L1N44Y01V TEXT:"triumph"] two weeks ago in Saxony-Anhalt. The AfD also recorded its best-ever result in Berlin, where the far-left Left Party came first and looks set to replace Merz's conservative Christian Democrats (CDU) in the mayor's office. Merz called the result in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania — the worst in CDU history — "a disaster". But he defied speculation he might step down, pledging to remain to pass a package of tax and pension reforms that he hopes will help revive Germany's sluggish economy. For now, at least, the party has stood behind him, although the result will add to pressure within his coalition with the centre-left Social Democrats (SPD), some of whom want to water down parts of the reform agenda. "We have to analyse, as a government, why there is this sense of uncertainty in the country," SPD co-leader Lars Klingbeil said. A pervasive sense of economic malaise and disillusion with traditional political parties point to further turbulence ahead, with a raft of state elections in western Germany due next year. "Germany is entering a period of political instability where viable coalitions are harder and harder to build, and that doesn't bode well for Europe when Germany is the de facto leader," said Sudha David-Wilp, a senior fellow at the German Marshall Fund of the United States. The AfD wants to expel foreigners with no right to stay in Germany, restore energy ties with Russia and quit the euro, while the Left Party wants to cap rents and nationalise large parts of the Berlin housing market. By contrast, Merz's pursuit of what he says are painful but necessary reforms has yet to yield improvements that voters can feel. "We can see how difficult it is to win people over while in government and from the centre of society," said Stefan Evers, the CDU's lead candidate in Berlin. DISASTER Even [USN:L8N3WN0O8 TEXT:"before the election"], Merz's approval ratings were at a record low and his party has trailed the AfD in national polling for months. "People would tell us that as long as he had a say in things, we wouldn't vote for you," said one CDU election campaigner in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. From the start of his time in office, when a normally routine parliamentary vote to confirm him as chancellor turned into a [USN:L6N3RE0KX TEXT:"humiliation"] requiring a second round of voting, Merz has struggled to establish his authority. There have been repeated gaffes, from saying people in Germany needed to work longer hours to identifying as "middle class" while working as a highly remunerated supervisory board chairman of asset management firm BlackRock. Surveys indicate that his communication lapses and his difficulty in establishing an emotional connection with voters anxious about their economic future both contributed to the outcome of all five state elections this year. But Germany's deep-seated economic challenges — an ageing population, poor growth and the erosion of its industrial base under increasing pressure from China — resist easy solutions. The reforms themselves caused problems in formerly communist eastern Germany, where despite more than three decades of economic transformation, more voters than in the west earn the minimum wage and rely completely on the state pension in retirement. Manuela Schwesig, the SPD state premier of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, whose success in limiting the AfD's gains in her state was one of the few bright spots for the government, said she was "surprised" by Merz's refusal to change course. Her campaign was heavily critical of Merz, whom she accused of showing indifference towards voters struggling with soaring fuel prices. She also called for changes to the pension reform that would require people to work for longer — a particularly unpopular issue in the east, where many have not built up the same level of savings as those in the west. FIREWALL UNDER PRESSURE Days before the vote, as speculation grew that his position might be in danger, [USN:S8N4130DH TEXT:"senior CDU leaders"] rallied around the chancellor, aware that replacing him would put the reform programme at risk without solving underlying problems. So far, the policy — known as the 'firewall' — under which the mainstream parties refuse to cooperate with the AfD has kept it from sharing power. But there are growing doubts about whether it is possible to exclude a party which enjoys the support of more voters in Germany than any other. Despite reservations about cooperating with a party with elements that are classified by the domestic security services as extremist right-wing, there are growing calls in the CDU for a rethink. "This 'firewall' hasn't done anything for the CDU and they need to think about that," said Leif-Erik Holm, the AfD's lead candidate in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. Opinion polls have shown deep disillusion among many voters with a political system that has seen a succession of coalitions between the formerly fiercely antagonistic mainstream parties of the centre-right and centre-left. Under former Chancellor Angela Merkel, the "grand coalition" of CDU and SPD, seen only once before at federal level during the 1960s, became standard. Merz, once seen as a firebrand conservative, repeated the exercise after another coalition, headed by SPD Chancellor Olaf Scholz, collapsed in 2024. "It's just allowed a vacuum on the right and the left for these parties to emerge," David-Wilp said.

item.title: Houthis push for control of Yemen highlands as Trump is said to have called off strikes
item.description: US President Donald Trump reportedly called off the airstrikes at the last minute, even as troops were loading bombs onto aircraft.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

Houthis push for control of Yemen highlands as Trump is said to have called off strikes

US President Donald Trump reportedly called off the airstrikes at the last minute, even as troops were loading bombs onto aircraft.

Iran-aligned Houthi fighters fire from their position in a screengrab from a video said to show Houthi fighters attacking Saudi-backed forces in the location given by the source as al Jawf governorate, Yemen, in this screengrab taken from a video released by Houthi Military Media on Sep 15, 2026. (Image: HOUTHI MILITARY MEDIA/Handout via REUTERS)

21 Sep 2026 07:49PM (Updated: 21 Sep 2026 11:32PM)

FAST

DUBAI: Houthi fighters pushed to seize strategic heights in Yemen on Monday (Sep 21) to cut off the Red Sea coast from remaining areas held by Saudi-backed forces, after a report that President Donald Trump had called off US strikes on the group at the last minute. A lightning advance by the Iran-backed group this month has extended the wider Middle East conflict to a new theatre and further threatened global energy supplies. Washington has so far rebuffed repeated pleas from Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to join the fight in Yemen.  Saudi Arabia has not commented on the first apparent strikes on the capital since the escalation began.

The New York Times reported that the Trump administration had prepared on Sunday to launch airstrikes against the Houthis after fresh pleas from the Saudi crown prince. But the newspaper said Trump called off the airstrikes at the last minute, even as troops were loading bombs onto aircraft. Reuters could not immediately verify the Times' report. The US military's Central Command referred questions to the White House. The White House did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment. Rashid al-Alimi, the Riyadh-based president of Yemen's Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government, asked Trump by phone on Sunday for US military help, four sources told Reuters.  Two of the sources, one Yemeni and one Western, said Trump made no direct pledge of support during the call. Riyadh was apparently struck on Saturday for the first time since the escalation began, with explosions heard and smoke visible near the airport. The Houthis said they had fired missiles at the Saudi capital ; the Saudis have not commented.

A fighter jet sits on the flight deck of the USS George Washington in the Arabian Sea, on Sep 11, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Ed Ou)

FIGHTING IN HIGHLANDS The Houthis, who have controlled Yemen's capital since 2014, seized the country's Red Sea coast this month in an advance that routed forces of the Saudi-backed government. Saudi Arabia has launched hundreds of strikes in recent days on the fighters' positions in the highlands, the Houthis say. According to the United Nations, nearly 700 people have been killed and thousands injured in the flare-up in fighting. Nearly 130,000 Yemenis have fled homes within Yemen, and more than 3,000 have fled by boat across the Red Sea to Africa. Five Yemeni military sources told Reuters the Houthis were now seeking to seize strategic heights, known as the Kahboub Mountains, in two provinces, Taiz and Lahij, which separate the Red Sea coast from the government-held south. Fighting has centred on the outskirts of the remote mountain Al-Wazi'iyah district in Taiz province, and Ras al-Ara along the Indian Ocean coast between the mouth of the Red Sea that the fighters captured last week and the government's base in Aden. "The government forces appear to remain largely in a defensive posture following the loss of the Bab el-Mandeb area, while the Houthis are seeking to maintain the momentum of their advance, despite being exposed to intensive air strikes," said Mohammed Al-Qadhi, a veteran Yemeni journalist now working as a political analyst. "These mountains could become critical to determining whether the Houthis succeed in consolidating their recent territorial gains or whether government forces will be able to retain the positions necessary to mount a counteroffensive."

A drone view of a camp for internally displaced people, who fled fighting between the Houthis and government forces in Red Sea coastline areas, erected near Aden, Yemen, on Sep 19, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Stringer)

SAUDI OIL EXPORTS The surge in fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis creates a dilemma for Trump, under pressure to help defend Washington's Saudi allies but anxious not to further expand the deeply unpopular war he launched in February against Iran. The United States bombed the Houthis for two months in early 2025, but Trump called off those strikes after reaching a ceasefire with the group and has kept out of the conflict since. The Houthis' newfound control of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait risks cutting off the main alternative route that Saudi Arabia has used for oil exports that bypass disruption in the Strait of Hormuz. Saudi Arabia has responded by increasing shipments through Hormuz, where a small number of tankers are increasingly shuttling back and forth to bring out oil, charging record fees of as much as a quarter of the value of the cargo to brave the wartime risk. They then transfer the oil to other ships in the Indian Ocean, bound for customers in Asia or elsewhere. Traders say Saudi Arabia has sold 60 million barrels of oil both this month and next, to be loaded from off Oman on the far side of Hormuz. Satellite data shows Saudi exports through Hormuz reaching 2.9 million barrels per day in recent days, up from just 700,000 in August. That has helped put a cap on the global price of crude, which has retreated closer to US$100 a barrel after approaching US$110 last week. But consumers and industries are still paying record prices for some refined fuels, with the US retail price of diesel hitting another all-time high on Monday. In the latest reported attack in Hormuz, Britain's UKMTO maritime security agency said a ship sailing into the strait had been hit with a projectile, causing minor injuries to the crew. It also said it had learned of an earlier strike on a gas tanker. Diplomacy in the wider conflict has largely been stalled since a June interim agreement between the United States and Iran collapsed within weeks. Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian is due to fly on Tuesday to New York to attend the UN General Assembly , the first such visit since Trump launched "Operation Epic Fury" against his country alongside Israel in February.

item.title: トルコ、ファンド業界幹部の資産を凍結－混乱対応で取り締まり強化
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： トルコは投資会社数社の幹部に関連する資産を凍結し、ファンド業界に対する捜査を拡大した。一部ファンドが顧客の解約請求に応じられなかったことをきっかけに、同国では株価が急落するなど混乱が広がっていた。

ギュルレク法相がXへの投稿で明らかにしたところによると、同国投資会社のテラ・ヤティリム・メンクル・デエルエル、プスラ・フィナンス・ホールディング、ヘデフ・ホールディング、ブルス・ポルトフォイ・ヨネティミなどに関係する幹部の資産が対象。当局はまた、取締役や代表権者、その一部の親族に関係する資産の移転を検察当局の承認なしには行えないよう制限する措置も講じた。

ファンド業界の混乱を受けて規制当局は7社が運用する131本のファンドに清算を命じたが、今回の措置で取り締まりを一段と強化した。

ギュルレク氏によると、25人に対して司法手続きが開始され、このうち15人は身柄を拘束された。「逃亡中の容疑者10人には、拘束に向け行方を追っている」と付け加えた。

21日の取引では、トルコの代表的な株価指数であるイスタンブール100種指数が下落。下落率は一時3%近くに達した。同指数に入っていない中小の銘柄は売り直され、100近くの銘柄がストップ安となる10%安に沈んでいる。

テラとプスラの大型ファンドが保有していた銘柄も、急落が続いている。テラ系列の金融サービス会社デステクは全株指数の下落に大きく寄与。同社会長は株価急騰によってトルコ有数の富豪となっていたが、逮捕されたと現地メディアが報じた。

事情に詳しい関係者が18日に明らかにしたところによると、トルコの政府系ファンドは先週、国営証券会社ジラート・ポルトフォイが運用する同国の上場企業大手30社に連動する上場取引型商品を通じ、株式を買い支えた。

資本市場委員会（CMB）は20日夜、対象ファンドの清算期間を3カ月から6カ月に延長した。この変更について、資産を「可能な限り有利な条件で」売却できるようにすることが目的だと説明した。

item.title: 旺盛な需要もインフレ圧力、利上げ対応に合理性とシカゴ連銀総裁
item.description:
Howard Schneider
［ワシントン ２１日 ロイター］ - 米シカゴ地区連銀のグールズビー総裁は２１日、米...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
旺盛な需要もインフレ圧力、利上げ対応に合理性とシカゴ連銀総裁 9/21 20:48 配信

ワイオミング州ジャクソンホールで8月撮影　REUTERS/Ann Saphir

Howard Schneider

［ワシントン　２１日　ロイター］ - 米シカゴ地区連銀のグールズビー総裁は２１日、米国のインフレは過去１８カ月間の関税やエネルギー価格によるショックだけでなく、旺盛な需要によっても押し上げられている可能性があるとし、そうであれば、より高い金利が必要になることに「あいまいさはない」と述べた。

グールズビー総裁は、ロンドンで開催される公的通貨金融機関フォーラム（ＯＭＦＩＦ）向けに用意した講演原稿で、「需要が過熱すれば、ＦＲＢがどう対応する必要があるかにあいまいさはない」と指摘した。人工知能（ＡＩ）分野への投資水準が「本来の範囲を超えて波及し、経済が吸収できる以上に総需要を押し上げている」可能性があると述べた。

また、理論上、インフレへの影響が一時的かつ一過性にとどまるはずの供給ショックが、より持続的な影響を及ぼしていることが明らかになっていると指摘し、中央銀行として金融政策を決定する際に、こうした影響を無視できないとした。

一般的には、供給不足や供給網のボトルネックが生じても、産業の生産は必然的に回復するため、供給ショックはおおむね自己修正的であり、政策当局はこれを見過ごすべきだと考えられている。しかし、コロナ禍以降は、供給ショックの発生頻度が高まり、期間も長期化している。

グールズビー氏は「原油、関税、コモディティー価格を巡り、予測担当者はインフレ率がいつピークを付けて低下し始めるかについて、１年以上にわたり見通し時期を先送りしてきた」とし、「安心できる傾向ではない」と述べた。

その上で「これらのショックが実際に弱まりつつある証拠が必要だ。そうでなければ、インフレ率を２％に戻す信頼できる道筋を見いだすのは難しく、こうしたショックを見過ごし続けることがますます難しくなる」とした。

インフレ率は直近で３．７％とＦＲＢの目標２％を上回っており、改善がほとんどみられていない。

グールズビー氏は「そのような状況では、元に戻るには困難な手段しかない」と述べ、金利を引き上げ、景気減速に伴う成長や雇用へのリスクを受け入れる必要があるとした。

グールズビー氏は今年の連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）で投票権を持たない。０．２５％ポイントの利上げを決定した９月１５─１６日の会合の結果や自身の金融政策見通しについてはコメントしなかった。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：米景気拡大維持、ＦＲＢの利下げペース次第 アングル：米長期金利5％接近で株式市場に警戒感、決算後はマクロ要因に注目 焦点：ベセント氏発言で強まる日銀9月利上げ観測、米国の影響力拡大に懸念も アングル：米国債「ツイスト・スティープ化」、ＦＲＢの信認巡る懸念反映か アングル：インフレで揺らぐ債券のヘッジ機能、米投資家は実物資産に移行 最終更新: 9/21(月) 20:48 ロイター

item.title: Cobre sube mientras expectativas sobre demanda china se suman a impulso especulativo
item.description: Los precios del cobre subieron el lunes por quinta sesión consecutiva, acercándose a máximos históricos, ya que las expectativas de un repunte estacional de la demanda en China —el mayor consumidor mundial— mantuvieron las compras especulativas.
item.dc:creator: Polina Devitt
item.content:encoded: Los precios del cobre subieron el lunes por quinta sesión consecutiva, acercándose a máximos históricos, ya que las expectativas de un repunte estacional de la demanda en China —el mayor consumidor mundial— mantuvieron las compras especulativas. * El contrato de referencia del cobre a tres meses en la Bolsa de Metales de Londres (LME) ganó un 1%, a 14.669,5 dólares por tonelada, a las 1612 GMT, tras alcanzar los 14.774 dólares, su nivel más alto desde el 10 de septiembre, cuando tocó un máximo de 14.875 dólares. * La renovada demanda especulativa ha impulsado al alza el precio del cobre después de que los fondos redujeran sus posiciones largas netas en los futuros de la Comex en la semana que finalizó el 15 de septiembre, ya que la Casa Blanca aún no se ha pronunciado sobre los aranceles al cobre refinado, según explicó Ole Hansen, de Saxo Bank. * La prima de los futuros del cobre en Estados Unidos sobre los precios de la LME se amplió, volviendo a subir hacia niveles que fomentan nuevos envíos físicos a las existencias de la Comex , que almacenan el 69% del millón de toneladas de existencias supervisadas por la bolsa. * Las expectativas de reposición de existencias en China antes de las festividades del 25 de septiembre y del 1 al 7 de octubre sirvieron de apoyo a los precios del cobre, mientras los operadores esperan la cita de esta semana entre el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, y su par chino, Xi Jinping. * Las existencias de cobre disponibles en los almacenes registrados en la LME cayeron a 133.725 toneladas, según mostraron los datos diarios de la LME, tras registrarse 9.600 toneladas de nuevas cancelaciones en Asia. * Esto contribuyó a ampliar la prima del contrato al contado de cobre de la LME sobre el índice de referencia hasta los 46 dólares por tonelada, frente al descuento de 86 dólares registrado el 14 de septiembre. * En otros metales básicos, el aluminio cayó un 0,6%, a 3.267 dólares la tonelada; el zinc ganó un 0,3%, a 3.930 dólares; el plomo avanzó un 0,8%, a 1.936,5 dólares, tras alcanzar su máximo de tres meses en 1.942 dólares; el estaño mejoró un 0,5%, a 53.940 dólares; y el níquel avanzó un 1,3%, a 16.385 dólares.

item.title: 22日にグリーンランド協定署名へ、安保でＮＡＴＯ関与
item.description:
Stine Jacobsen Jacob Gronholt-Pedersen
［コペンハーゲン ２１日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Stine Jacobsen　Jacob Gronholt-Pedersen

［コペンハーゲン　２１日　ロイター］ - 米国、デンマーク、デンマーク自治領グリーンランドは２２日にニューヨークでグリーンランドの安全保障に関する協定に署名する見通しだ。デンマークは、この合意により北極圏の安全保障は米国とデンマークだけが担うのではなく、北大西洋条約機構（ＮＡＴＯ）の監視下に置かれると説明している。

合意は２２日にニューヨークで開かれる国連総会で署名される見通しだが、内容は公表されておらず、米国軍のグリーンランド駐留の法的根拠となっている１９５１年の防衛協定を改定するかどうかなどは不明。

デンマークのラスムセン外相は２０日、テレビ局ＴＶ２に対し、「合意は北極圏の安全保障に対する責任が、デンマークまたは米国だけにあるものではない形になる」と述べ、大部分は「ＮＡＴＯが北極圏を担うことになる」とした。

トランプ米大統領は１８日、グリーンランドの安全保障などについてデンマーク、グリーンランドと合意に達したと明らかにし、合意により米国が「恒久的な管理権」を得ると主張した。

グリーンランドは１９日、米国との合意はグリーンランドの主権を損なうものではないとの立場を示した。ＮＡＴＯ報道官は１９日、この合意を歓迎すると表明。「極めて重要なこの地域の安全、安定、協力の促進に寄与する」と述べた。

トランプ氏は、グリーンランドは米国が管理すべきだと主張し、軍事力や経済力を行使する可能性を排除しない姿勢を示してきた。圧力は１月にピークに達し、ＮＡＴＯ内の外交危機を招いた。デンマークとグリーンランドは圧力の緩和を目指し、米政府との交渉に入った。

item.title: Smart ring maker Oura eyes $15.6 billion IPO valuation in fall listings demand test
item.description: Oura kicked off the roadshow for its US initial public offering on Monday, targeting a fully-diluted valuation of $15.62 billion as the smart ring maker tests investor appetite for consumer technology companies after a tepid start to the fall IPO season.
item.dc:creator: Manya Saini
item.content:encoded: Oura kicked off the roadshow for its US initial public offering on Monday, targeting a fully-diluted valuation of $15.62 billion as the smart ring maker tests investor appetite for consumer technology companies after a tepid start to the fall IPO season. The IPO, expected sometime next week, comes as markets have been on edge in recent weeks over uncertainty around the AI trade, rising bond yields and a shifting Federal Reserve rate outlook. Oura and some of its existing investors plan to raise as much as $2.2 billion through the sale of 50 million shares at the top of the indicated price range of $40 to $44. "Oura is the first real test of US appetite after a sluggish September so far and a period of more volatile markets. If it comes strongly out the gate, it will encourage other issuers," said Samuel Kerr, global head of equity capital markets at Mergermarket. "However, a weaker IPO might set alarm bells ringing that market sentiment may be turning." Weight-loss drugmaker Eli Lilly (LLY.N) has indicated interest in purchasing up to $100 million of the shares, while investment firm Dragoneer has indicated interest in buying up to $300 million worth of shares. PRICES IN DEMAND FOR HIGH-TECH HEALTH MONITORS Smart rings are carving out a niche between traditional fitness trackers and smartwatches, capitalizing on demand for personalized wellness insights while offering a smaller, screen-free way to monitor health round the clock with a longer battery life. Oura has helped popularize the device, which tracks metrics such as heart health, activity and sleep. The health-tech company sold 3.6 million Oura Rings in the 12 months ended June 30, according to its IPO prospectus. Its revenue for the nine months ended June 30 surged roughly 74% year-over-year to $1.21 billion. The company expects to end fiscal 2026 with roughly 5.7 million paid members, representing 96% growth over the prior year. "One of Oura's strengths is that it is beginner friendly, fashionable and feels more like an easy add-on to everyday life, compared with some wearables that are more geared toward serious athletes and performance tracking," Kat Liu, vice president at IPOX, said. "The valuation is clearly pricing in continued strong growth and a further shift toward higher-margin recurring revenue." The company, founded over a decade ago in Finland, reached a valuation of about $11 billion in a late-stage funding round last year. Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and J.P. Morgan are the lead underwriters of the IPO. The company is expected to price its IPO and begin trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "OURA" next week.

item.title: Air taxi maker Vertical taps former Airbus executive Fabrice Bregier as chair
item.description: Air taxi developer Vertical Aerospace said on Monday it had appointed former Airbus Commercial Aircraft division chief executive Fabrice Bregier as chair of its board of directors.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Air taxi developer Vertical Aerospace said on Monday it had appointed former Airbus (AIR.PA) Commercial Aircraft division chief executive Fabrice Bregier as chair of its board of directors. Here are some more details: The announcement comes as electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft firms race to secure regulatory approvals ahead of commercial launches. Alongside its all-electric, four-passenger piloted aircraft Valo, Vertical is developing a hybrid-electric variant, which would offer more range and mission flexibility. EVTOL firms are also focusing more on the military market amid rising defense spending, with commercial development taking longer than expected. Bregier most recently served as president of Palantir Technologies (PLTR.O) France from 2018 to 2024. In addition to serving as CEO of Airbus' unit from 2012 to 2018, Bregier was chief operating officer of the group, where he led the development of the A350 programme and the company's operational turnaround. Vertical said Ben Story, who has been the company's interim chair since May, would remain a member of the board. Shares of the company were marginally down in afternoon trading.

item.title: 中国共産党、10月26─29日に5中総会開催へ－党統治の厳格化を協議
item.description:
（ブルームバーグ）： 中国共産党は10月26─29日、党の自己統治を巡る問題を検討する重要会議を開く。共産党の習近平総書記（国家主席）が4期目続投を固めると見込まれる来秋の党大会に向け、カウントダウンが始まる。
国営の新華社通信によると、中央政治局は21日の月例会議終了後、いわゆる中央委員会第5回総会（5中総会）の日程を発表した。
党中央委員会の委員約400人が北京に集まる。新華社によれば、「全面的かつ厳格な党の自己統治の推進に関する重大な問題」を検討し、決定する。
新華社は、党の長期政権を確保するため、「党建設が直面する顕著な問題に効果的に対処し、解決しなければならない」と伝えた。詳細には触れなかった。
中国が地方と中央の双方で大規模な人事刷新を控える中、今回の会議では、党幹部への監督強化と汚職根絶を目指す習氏の取り組みが今後どのような方向に進むのか、その手掛かりが注目される。
原題：Xi to Convene

item.title: Gaza students return to in-person schooling for first time in three years
item.description: Hundreds of thousands of children in Gaza returned to in-person teaching on Saturday for the first time in nearly three years, albeit in damaged or makeshift school buildings and tents, and with uniforms, notebooks and pens unaffordable for many families.
item.dc:creator: Nidal Al-Mughrabi, Haseeb, Alwazeer
item.content:encoded: Hundreds of thousands of children in Gaza returned to in-person teaching on Saturday for the first time in nearly three years, albeit in damaged or makeshift school buildings and tents, and with uniforms, notebooks and pens unaffordable for many families. The United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) says 98% of schools in Gaza were either destroyed or damaged during the war, and Gaza education officials say about 660,000 students have been deprived of in-person learning and regular participation in education. The reopening is a fragile milestone for Gaza after a conflict that has killed around 22,000 students and more than 770 education workers, including 532 teachers, according to Ibrahim Ramadan, director of education for East Khan Younis. "The last time I have been to school was three years ago. Now, we are starting the school year, it is year of joy, happiness and success," said Moayed Abu Mustafa in Khan Younis. Mustafa said he was determined to learn even though he will sit on the floor in a tent lacking ventilation, he has no decent shoes, nor a notebook and pen, and lost friends during the war. "Despite all of this we will learn, we will learn even in a tent." Fifteen-year-old displaced student Samar Abu Salmi, who lives with her family in a tent, is also returning to class. "We studied on phones and we haven’t seen our teachers... now, we are back pursuing our dream... from one tent to another," she said, speaking in the yard of her new makeshift school. She also lacks much of the essential equipment, which has become unaffordable for her family. "Before the war, everything was available for us - notebooks, pens, goods, clothes, outings, things that we could get cheaply," Salmi said. MATTRESSES AND A BLACKBOARD Despite the devastation in the enclave, the Ministry of Education, backed by international and local organisations, has moved ahead with the 2026-27 academic year, establishing dozens of temporary schools made of tents, tarpaulins, sheet metal and wood to accommodate pupils. Some are built on sandy ground, others have classrooms with only some mattresses and a blackboard, into which students cram. Others are still housing dozens of displaced families. Attending another school was 14-year-old Yamen Abu Samra. "We used to wake up happy to go to school... Now, when we come to school, we’re afraid of stray bullets, rockets, strikes, everything," he said. "Now, I’m sitting in a tent that has absolutely nothing, just the sun and the heat," he added. At least 540,000 students are expected to attend in-person classes this year in makeshift private schools, temporary learning centres and educational points, with UNICEF support, according to education officials. Online learning will continue for those who can't attend classes or who left Gaza during the war. Israeli forces remain in control of more than 60% of Gaza despite last year's ceasefire, which halted major fighting but failed to end the conflict. Palestinian authorities say more than 73,000 people have been killed in Israel's assault on Gaza, launched after Hamas-led fighters killed about 1,200 people in southern Israel in October 2023. Stationery trader Khaled Aliyan, 30, said Israeli import restrictions have reduced supplies and hiked prices. "This notebook, which used to cost 3 shekels ($1), now costs 15 (shekels). All stationery items are expensive," he said. Israel's COGAT military agency, which controls access to Gaza, did not respond to a Reuters request for comment on restrictions on supplies and strikes on schools. Israel has repeatedly accused Hamas of using schools for military purposes, which Hamas denies. ($1 = 3.0177 shekels)

item.title: 独自動車労働者が抗議、業績悪化のＶＷ非難 ポルシェは追加削減報道否定
item.description:
Christoph Steitz Rachel More
［フランクフルト／ベルリン ２１日 ロイター］ - ドイツで...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
独自動車労働者が抗議、業績悪化のＶＷ非難　ポルシェは追加削減報道否定 9/21 19:53 配信

フォルクスワーゲンの電気自動車生産拠点であるドイツ・エムデン工場で2025年2月撮影 REUTERS/Carmen Jaspersen/File Photo

Christoph Steitz　Rachel More

［フランクフルト／ベルリン　２１日　ロイター］ - ドイツで２１日、自動車労働者が全国規模の抗議行動を行った。フォルクスワーゲン（ＶＷ）が１８日に高級スポーツカー部門ポルシェでの６０億ユーロ（６８億８０００万ドル）ののれん代減損を含む業績予想下方修正を発表。１９日には、ポルシェを巡り、ＶＷの大規模再建計画に４０００人超の追加削減案が含まれていると独経済紙ハンデルスブラットが報じた。

抗議はＶＷ、ＢＭＷ、部品供給大手ボッシュで行われた。ドイツにとって最も重要な産業である自動車業界は、痛みを伴う人員削減、生産移転、工場閉鎖の可能性に直面。危機の影響は２０日の州議会選挙の結果にも表れた。

ＶＷは今月、過去最大規模の事業再建策で合意。新たに５万人を削減する計画で、強力な労組との全面対立は回避した。

しかし、労組側は経営陣に問題解決を求める姿勢を改めて示した。

フォルクスワーゲンのダニエラ・カバロ従業員代表委員長と、金属産業労組ＩＧメタルのクリスティアネ・ベナー委員長は、中国との不公正な競争に対する保護の強化、より効果的な欧州連合（ＥＵ）の補助金政策、段階的退職制度の継続を要求。

ベナー氏は、ウォルフスブルクのフォルクスワーゲン本社で従業員に対し、「企業の指導者と経営陣には、自動車生産国としてのドイツ、従業員、雇用に責任を持つことを期待する」と述べた。

ＩＧメタルのホルスト・オット氏は「怠慢と壊滅的な判断ミスにより、ほとんどの経営者は電動モビリティー、デジタル化、電池技術の進展に追随できず、ドイツの自動車・部品産業を後退させた」と批判した。

一方、４０００人の追加人員削減計画が報じられたポルシェのミヒャエル・ライタース最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は従業員に対し、報道を否定した。

ライタース氏はロイターが２１日に確認した内部メモで「ポルシェで追加で４０００人の雇用を削減する計画はない」と表明。既存の再編計画はポルシェの監査役会で承認されているとし、「計画のいかなる変更も想定していない」と述べた。

item.title: Oro cae por apuestas alcistas sobre tasas de la Fed y fortaleza del dólar
item.description: Los precios del oro bajaban el lunes, en una sesión en la que las expectativas de un mayor endurecimiento de la política monetaria por parte de la Reserva Federal este año y las señales de línea dura de otros bancos centrales importantes fortalecían al dólar.
item.dc:creator: Anjana Anil
item.content:encoded: Los precios del oro bajaban el lunes, en una sesión en la que las expectativas de un mayor endurecimiento de la política monetaria por parte de la Reserva Federal este año y las señales de línea dura de otros bancos centrales importantes fortalecían al dólar. * A las 1540 GMT, el oro al contado cayó un 0,6%, a 4.350,39 dólares por onza, tras perder más de un 1% más temprano, a un mínimo de sesión de 4.322,19 dólares. Los futuros del oro en Estados Unidos restaban un 0,8%, a 4.388,4 dólares. * El dólar se apreciaba frente a una cesta de seis destacadas monedas, ampliando las ganancias tras el alza de tasas de interés de la Fed, que lo impulsó más de un 1% la semana pasada. Un billete verde más fuerte encarece el oro para los tenedores de otras divisas. * "Vemos cierta preocupación persistente entre los alcistas por el endurecimiento de la política monetaria estadounidense, lo que impulsó al índice dólar a un máximo en más de dos meses el viernes. Esos factores bajistas están jugando en contra de los metales preciosos", dijo Jim Wyckoff, de American Gold Exchange. * Según la herramienta FedWatch de CME, los operadores ven una probabilidad del 88% de una subida de tasas en diciembre. El oro suele considerarse una cobertura contra la inflación, pero pierde atractivo frente a los activos que generan rendimiento en un entorno de tipos elevados. * La guerra de Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán ha impulsado al alza los precios de la energía, avivando los temores de inflación y reforzando las posturas restrictivas de los bancos centrales, lo que ha provocado que el oro haya caído un 17% desde su máximo de la sesión del 27 de febrero. * El presidente de la Fed de Mineápolis, Neel Kashkari, afirmó el domingo que la inflación es demasiado elevada en todos los sectores de la economía estadounidense, no solo en el del petróleo. * En otros metales preciosos, la plata al contado bajó un 0,1%, a 66,14 dólares; el platino subió un 0,2%, a 1.803,67 dólares; y el paladio ganó un 0,4%, a 1.306,93 dólares.

item.title: Drug developer ADARx seeks $1.74 billion valuation in US IPO
item.description: ADARx Pharmaceuticals, which develops RNA-based drugs for rare diseases, said on Monday that it was targeting a valuation of up to $1.74 billion, as it joins a wave of biotech companies planning for a US IPO.
item.dc:creator: Pragyan Kalita
item.content:encoded: ADARx Pharmaceuticals, which develops RNA-based drugs for rare diseases, said on Monday that it was targeting a valuation of up to $1.74 billion, as it joins a wave of biotech companies planning for a US IPO. Drugmaker AbbVie (ABBV.N) has agreed to invest up to $100 million in a concurrent private placement, which would give it a roughly 4.9% stake post-IPO, ADARx said. AbbVie had paid the company $335 million in May 2025 for a research collaboration. The investment provides external validation of ADARx's technology, said IPOX Research Associate Lukas Muehlbauer. ADARx's experimental drugs target diseases related to immunity, kidney, cardiovascular and neurological systems. Three of its programs are in clinical testing and two in advanced preclinical development. The company's most advanced candidate, onvuzosiran, is in late-stage testing for hereditary angioedema, a rare genetic disorder that causes sudden swelling attacks. San Diego-based ADARx, founded in 2019, is aiming to raise up to $371.9 million by offering 21.9 million shares priced between $15 and $17. BIOTECH MOMENTUM CONTINUES The IPO comes even as a sharp rise in Treasury yields and higher interest rates have nudged some prospective issuers to the sidelines, although biotech offerings have broadly rebounded from year-ago levels. Drug developers Retension Pharmaceuticals and TRex Bio filed for their listings on Friday while Electra Therapeutics (ETRA.O) debuted in the market after raising $350 million in an upsized IPO. According to Muehlbauer, however, the reopening of the biotech IPO market is still selective — favouring companies with later-stage assets, upcoming catalysts and exposure to areas such as obesity and oncology. "Sentiment has also been helped by big pharma's appetite for external innovation," he said. Prospects of acquisitions of even relatively new biotechs mean a potential route to returns for investors despite higher rates. JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, TD Cowen, among others, are the underwriters for the offering. It will list on the Nasdaq under the symbol "ADRX."

item.title: Morning Bid: Summiteering
item.description: After a turbulent week of central bank tightening, markets now turn to diplomacy - or at least top-level summits - as world leaders gather at the United Nations General Assembly in New York this week.
item.dc:creator: Mike Dolan
item.content:encoded: After a turbulent week of [USN:L1N45A09M TEXT:"central bank tightening"], markets now turn to diplomacy - or at least top-level summits - as world leaders gather at the United Nations General Assembly in New York this week. Topping the list of bilateral summits, though, is [USN:L8N45A068 TEXT:"Thursday's meeting"] between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington. Ahead of that, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and China's Vice Premier He Lifeng [USN:L1N45B04Y TEXT:"met on Sunday"] to prepare an agenda on trade relations, AI concerns and geopolitics. But the noisy backdrop of two raging wars in the Middle East and Eastern Europe competed for the weekend headlines, as both Saudi Arabia's capital [USN:S8N43F04S TEXT:"Riyadh"] and Russia's capital [USN:FWN45A0G8 TEXT:"Moscow"] came under attack from Iran-backed Houthis and Ukrainian forces, respectively. Oil prices did [USN:L4N45C04W TEXT:"slip back"] on Monday, however, on hopes that Saudi Arabia would restore some flows through its East-West pipeline and amid some reports that oil and fuel shipments had picked up in September. Observable data was [USN:L4N45D03T TEXT:"less optimistic"]. There were also some hopes that Chinese [USN:L8N4590LF TEXT:"pressure"] on Iran to rein in regional attacks may have some impact. Even though Brent crude remains above $100 per barrel and reports of some refined oil shortages were emerging at US retailers, stock markets welcomed the crude retreat and [USN:L4N45C05I TEXT:"were higher"] in thin trading on Monday. Japan has had little opportunity to react to Friday's Bank of Japan [USN:L4N4580GX TEXT:"interest rate rise"], as Tokyo markets are closed for much of this week for holidays. The yen pared some losses on Friday after a reported rate check, having [USN:L6N45A00Q TEXT:"weakened"] against the dollar following the hike. The currency was [USN:L4N45D01G TEXT:"steady"] on Monday amid some trepidation about further official intervention during the market closures. More broadly, rate markets were trying to calibrate 'what next' after the Federal Reserve's [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"rate rise"] last week. One more hike is now fully priced by year-end, and a move as soon as next month is about 50-50. Minneapolis Fed boss Neal Kashkari [USN:L1N45C03B TEXT:"said on Sunday"] that inflation concerns were not just about oil prices, with services price inflation just as worrying. Economists reckon the Fed is now trying to reset to absorb a faster-growing economy ahead that may prevent it hitting its inflation target. Two-year Treasury yields have jumped as much as 36 basis points in the past two weeks. Elsewhere, the Bank of England is also expected to raise rates by year-end, even after leaving policy [USN:L8N4590W3 TEXT:"unchanged"] last week. And European markets will eye another round of poor results for Germany's ruling CDU party in two weekend state elections, although German Chancellor Friedrich Merz [USN:L8N45D0G1 TEXT:"vowed to press on"] and the euro held steady first thing Monday. Chart of the day The French government must now pay a 104-basis-point premium on its 10-year bonds over Germany's [USN:L8N45A0ZG TEXT:"for the first time since 2012"], as investors seek more compensation to hold its debt. Investors, worried about long-term finances across developed economies, are growing concerned as France struggles to cut its high budget deficit ahead of a [USN:L1N45507C TEXT:"presidential election"] next year that could make that task even harder. The government is trying to reduce the shortfall from 5.4% of output this year to 5% next year through [USN:L8N4590SH TEXT:"€54 billion of tough spending cuts"]. Opposition parties are likely to challenge them in the coming months, potentially bringing the government down. Today's events to watch Chicago Fed's Austan Goolsbee speaks European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde and Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem also speak Japanese financial markets closed for holidays, returning Thursday Want to receive the Morning Bid in your inbox every weekday morning? DHAKA, Sept 21 : Bangladesh has raised fuel prices by up to 17.4 per cent, piling fresh pressure on consumers and businesses, as the government moved to stem mounting losses from surging global oil prices and higher shipping costs linked to the Middle East conflict. The new rates, effective from Monday, are expected to raise transportation and production costs across the import-dependent economy, adding to inflationary pressures at a time when industries, including the country's key garment export sector, are already grappling with an acute energy crunch. “Staying in business means staying competitive — the buyer who gets a product onto the shelf fastest and cheapest wins — and gas, power, and fuel costs all feed into that equation,” said Mohiuddin Rubel, additional managing director of Denim Expert Ltd, which supplies brands including H&M. The Energy Ministry said international fuel prices had more than doubled since March 2026, while freight charges had risen significantly because of regional instability.

Under the new rates, diesel prices rose 17.4 per cent to 135 taka ($1.11) per litre from 115 taka. Prices of 95-octane gasoline increased to 165 taka per litre from 145 taka, petrol rose to 160 taka from 140 taka, while kerosene increased to 155 taka from 135 taka. The latest increase follows fuel price hikes in April and June, when the government also raised prices to help offset rising import costs driven by higher global oil prices. The ministry said state-owned Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation incurred losses of 228.76 billion taka ($1.9 billion) between March and August and that the latest price hike could cut annual losses by about 100 billion taka, while conserving foreign exchange reserves and curbing fuel smuggling to neighbouring countries where prices are higher. The ministry also cited substantial subsidies for liquefied natural gas, saying the government continued to support electricity and gas supplies despite higher import costs stemming from the regional energy crisis. The move drew concern from exporters, who said higher fuel costs would further squeeze manufacturers already battling energy shortages. "The fuel price hike will hurt everyone, from common people to businesses and industries. It will fuel inflation, increase production and transportation costs, trigger job losses and force some businesses to downsize," said Anwar-ul Alam Chowdhury, president of the Bangladesh Chamber of Industries. "The move will add pressure across the economy, including on manufacturers already struggling with energy shortages and thin margins," said Chowdhury, who is also the chairman of garment exporter Evince Group. ($1 = 122.1000 taka)

item.title: Poland watchdog fines Neuca in decade-long drug pricing cartel
item.description: Poland's competition regulator UOKiK said on Monday it fined pharmaceutical wholesaler Neuca 499 million zlotys ($131 million) for participating in a pricing cartel that lasted more than a decade, sending its shares sharply lower.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Poland's competition regulator UOKiK said on Monday it fined pharmaceutical wholesaler Neuca (NEUP.WA) 499 million zlotys ($131 million) for participating in a pricing cartel that lasted more than a decade, sending its shares sharply lower. The penalty was the largest in a total 905 million zloty fine against four wholesalers that shared drug pricing data for more than 10 years, UOKiK said. The regulator added that the three largest groups controlled more than 70% of Poland's wholesale drug market. • Neuca said it disagrees entirely with the charges and plans to appeal to Poland's Court of Competition and Consumer Protection. • UOKiK said wholesalers accessed pharmacy purchasing data through loyalty programmes, allowing them to see rivals' prices and terms for individual pharmacies and adjust their own offers. • As of 1045 GMT, shares of the company were down 15.6%, on track for the highest single-day fall ever. • Polska Grupa Farmaceutyczna avoided any financial penalty by cooperating with investigators under UOKiK's leniency program and providing evidence. • The decision is not final and companies may appeal to court. ($1 = 3.7921 zlotys)

ROME, Sept 21 : Pope Leo, who has warned of the risk that AI could lead the world down a path of unending war, on Monday urged the development of AI systems that do not foster divisions in society but strengthen peace initiatives. "In a world marked by conflict and division, the development of artificial intelligence calls for a vision inspired by wisdom and charity," the pontiff said in a message to a conference on AI issues held in Rome. The pope called for development of AI systems that "serve the dignity of every person and strengthen the bonds that unite the human family". Leo, the first US-born pope, has made addressing the possible dangers of AI development a major theme of his 16-month-old papacy, first discussing the issue publicly on his third day as pope.

item.title: UK indexes climb as oil prices retreat, banks lead gains
item.description: London shares closed higher on Monday, with banks leading gains, as risk appetite worldwide got a boost after oil prices retreated on hopes of diplomatic progress in the Middle East.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: London shares closed higher on Monday, with banks leading gains, as risk appetite worldwide got a boost after oil prices retreated on hopes of diplomatic progress in the Middle East. The blue-chip FTSE 100 index (.FTSE) rose 0.75% to 10,739.01 points after declining almost 1.5% in the previous session. The midcap FTSE 250 (.FTMC) climbed 1.18% to its highest level in nearly two weeks. Heavyweight banks (.FTNMX301010) were among the top gainers, with HSBC (HSBA.L) climbing 1.4%, Barclays (BARC.L) gaining 1.9% and Standard Chartered (STAN.L) rising 1.7%. The Aerospace and defence sector (.FTNMX502010) rose 2.8%, with Rolls-Royce (RR.L) gaining 3.8% and BAE Systems inching up 1.2%. Copper prices rose for a fifth straight session, approaching record highs as hopes of stronger Chinese demand fueled buying. Miners Antofagasta (ANTO.L) and Anglo American (AAL.L) jumped about 3.2% and 2.9%, respectively. Oil prices slid towards the psychological threshold of $100 a barrel and to their lowest in 11 days as investors hoped for diplomatic progress in resolving the Iran war ahead of this week's UN meeting. Energy stocks (.FTNMX601010) were down 1.9%, with BP (BP.L) and Shell (SHEL.L) falling 2.8% and 1.4%, respectively. Declining crude prices also boosted travel-related companies, with airline operator IAG (ICAG.L) climbing 2.9%. Healthcare investment firm Syncona (SYNCS.L) leaped 5.2% after its portfolio company Beacon Therapeutics' Phase II/III VISTA trial met the US FDA-endorsed primary endpoint for gene therapy laru-zova. Craneware (CRW.L) plummeted 25.8% after the healthcare financial software firm cut its full-year revenue outlook. Meanwhile, investors [USN:L8N45A068 TEXT:"await this week's meeting"] between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping for clues on trade relations and economic outlook. "Hopes of improved relations between the world's two largest economies were boosted by U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent describing weekend discussions with Chinese officials as successful," AJ Bell investment director Russ Mould said. British government bond yields eased after jumping last week, while the pound dipped around 0.2% a week after the Bank of England kept interest rates unchanged.

FRANKFURT, Sept 21 : The European Central Bank launched a new service on Monday linking its payment system to blockchain-based financial markets and said it would invest some of its own money in digital securities. The moves reflect a broader effort by central banks to adapt to the growing use of blockchain in finance, whereby assets are issued and traded using shared digital ledgers instead of traditional infrastructure. The new service, known as Pontes, allows banks and investors to settle blockchain-based transactions using euros backed by the ECB, rather than stablecoins or other forms of private money. The ECB said a first group of users, including Deutsche Bank, Santander and clearing giant Clearstream, had completed onboarding and would be able to use Pontes from the start.

The platform would initially operate between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m. CET (0600-1400 GMT) on business days and expand its services over time. "This technology has the potential to make transactions faster and more efficient by bundling multiple steps of an asset's lifecycle... and enabling automation," the ECB said. ECB TO INVEST IN BONDS ON BLOCKCHAIN The central bank said it would also begin investing a tiny part of its €23 billion own funds in blockchain-based securities, focusing on highly rated, euro-denominated debt issued by public institutions. Last month, ECB board member Isabel Schnabel said central banks should "go on-chain", arguing this would reduce reliance on private alternatives. Other central banks are pursuing similar initiatives. The Swiss National Bank is running Project Helvetia, which uses a wholesale digital currency to settle transactions in securities. The Bank of England is testing blockchain use through its Digital Securities Sandbox. The ECB is also working on a digital euro for consumers, partly to wean the bloc off US credit cards, and aims to launch it in 2029.

FAST

Sept 21 : It is sometimes called "momnesia," "mommy brain," "pregnancy brain" or "baby brain" — the forgetfulness, mental fogginess and cognitive changes that many women may experience during pregnancy. For instance, a woman might walk into the kitchen and forget why she did, or perhaps misplace her car keys in the bathroom. Scientists know it is a real biological phenomenon, and now have found a possible explanation, identifying a specific brain circuit that becomes disrupted under the sustained high levels of estrogen that accompany pregnancy. They conducted experiments using laboratory mice designed to mimic the sustained elevated estrogen experienced during pregnancy, finding that this led to temporary memory impairment in the animals without mood changes. Underlying this in the mice, they found, was how the high estrogen affected a neuronal pathway between two brain structures — the hypothalamus, which acts as a control center and integrative hub, and the hippocampus, which is central to memory formation.

High estrogen increased the activity of hypothalamus neurons, which in turn suppressed activity in the hippocampus and impaired memory, they found. "Momnesia" becomes most evident in late pregnancy and may continue into the postpartum period but usually dissipates after childbirth. Short-term and long-term memory can be affected, including spatial, social and verbal memory such as having difficulty remembering names or words, or struggling to recall familiar information. "It is not serious or medically disabling, although it does affect daily functioning and confidence," said Dr. Zheng Sun, a professor of medicine at Baylor College of Medicine specializing in endocrinology and molecular biology and one of the leaders of the study published in the journal Science Bulletin. "Typical examples include forgetting why one entered a room, misplacing an item, losing the thread of a conversation or needing reminders for appointments. It is widespread. About 80 per cent of pregnant women notice those changes, but that figure largely reflects self-report and subjective experience rather than objective testing," Sun said. The findings suggest that the phenomenon does not represent a general decline in cognitive ability. "The important point is that pregnancy does not simply make someone 'less intelligent.' The effects appear to be more subtle and specific to certain cognitive tasks," said Dr. Yanlin He, director of the Brain Glycemic and Metabolism Control Laboratory at Louisiana State University's Pennington Biomedical Research Center and another of the study leaders. MOUSE EXPERIMENTS The mouse experiments shed light on what is happening in the brain. Estrogen is a hormone that governs a woman's pregnancy, menstrual cycle and puberty, spurring physical changes that help the body support the fetus, foster fetal development and prepare for childbirth. Its levels increase during pregnancy, peaking in the third trimester. The researchers found that a protein called "estrogen receptor alpha" transmits estrogen's signals into cells in the hypothalamus. This region has abundant brain cells called GABAergic neurons that typically transmit calming signals to other parts of the brain. The study showed that high estrogen levels over-activate the inhibitory signals by these neurons in the mice, and this directly affected the hippocampus. The researchers performed memory tests including object and location recognition, finding impairment in mice given high estrogen levels compared to those that were not. When the researchers experimentally turned off the hypothalamus-to-hippocampus neuronal pathway, the mice no longer experienced estrogen-induced memory problems. But experimentally activating the same pathway impaired memory in the mice, even without higher amounts of estrogen present. "When we genetically removed estrogen receptors from these hypothalamic neurons, estrogen-induced and pregnancy-induced memory problems in mice were also reversed. We suspect that a similar circuit may play a similar role in humans, although you cannot do this type of invasive study directly in humans," Sun said. The researchers complemented the mouse experiments with a study assessing memory performance in 70 women, including some across different stages of pregnancy and some who were not pregnant, using tests of long-term, short-term and working memory. These tests revealed memory impairments that manifested during late pregnancy, correlating with high circulating estrogen levels. "Importantly, higher circulating estrogen levels were associated with poorer performance on several memory-related measures even after accounting for other potential contributing factors. This provides human evidence consistent with the mechanism we identified in mice," He said. "However, we should emphasize that we did not directly manipulate or measure this specific neural circuit in pregnant women. Therefore, the human findings support the hypothesis but do not establish the same level of causality as the mouse experiments," He said.

Source: Reuters

item.title: New air traffic control failure delays flights at some UK airports
item.description: Manchester, Glasgow and Belfast airports were experiencing delays, and London's Gatwick and City Airports said there would be some disruption.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

New air traffic control failure delays flights at some UK airports

Manchester, Glasgow and Belfast airports were experiencing delays, and London's Gatwick and City Airports said there would be some disruption.

Passengers stand with their luggage underneath an information display board in the South Terminal of London Gatwick Airport near Crawley, southern England, on Sep 9, 2026, following the second day of major disruption due to an issue affecting the NATS air traffic control systems. (File photo: AFP/Justin Talls)

FAST

LONDON: Flights at several British airports were delayed on Monday (Sep 21) by an air traffic control failure, Britain's air traffic control provider NATS said, less than two weeks after a separate issue halted flights across the country . Manchester, Glasgow and Belfast airports experienced delays, which NATS said were related to an issue at its Prestwick centre in Scotland, while London Gatwick and London City airports said there would be some disruption. British transport minister Heidi Alexander, who has been considering the future of NATS Chief Executive Martin Rolfe after repeated failures, said the problem had now been fixed and systems were resuming. "I know this will be deeply frustrating for passengers after the previous issue," she said on X.

Ryanair, Europe's biggest airline, said 25,000 of its passengers were facing delays as a result of Monday's issue and repeated its calls for Rolfe to resign. Rival airline easyJet said it had cancelled some flights while British Airways warned its customers that they were likely to experience disruption on Monday. The Civil Aviation Authority said passengers were "unlikely to be entitled to compensation for delays or cancellations that were directly caused by the incident", though it said passengers should be looked after by airlines. NEW ISSUE BEHIND DELAYS NATS said that Monday's delays were caused by a connectivity issue "unrelated to the issue two weeks ago", when about 2,000 flights were cancelled owing to a software defect, affecting hundreds of thousands of people. Cancellations on Monday had reached 24 by 0858 GMT. "Airports south of Manchester are broadly unaffected, however flights heading north and flights departing Scottish airports are currently subject to some delay," a NATS statement said. A previous outage in August 2023 cost airlines £100 million (US$134 million) and caused travel chaos. EasyJet said that Monday's disruption underlined weakness in the air traffic operator's systems. "This, once again, calls into question the resilience of NATS' systems and demonstrates the need for firm actions to prevent these repeated failures," easyJet said.

item.title: 人民元、22年6月末以来の高値で通常取引終了 首脳会談控え上昇容認との声
item.description:
Jiaxing Li
［香港 ２１日 ロイター］ - 中国人民元は２１日の通常取引を１ドル＝６．６９５５元と、２０２２...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
人民元、22年6月末以来の高値で通常取引終了　首脳会談控え上昇容認との声 9/21 18:43 配信

タイ・バンコクの銀行で2023年1月撮影　REUTERS/Athit Perawongmetha

Jiaxing Li

［香港　２１日　ロイター］ - 中国人民元は２１日の通常取引を１ドル＝６．６９５５元と、２０２２年６月３０日以来の高値で終えた。今週の米中首脳会談を前に、中国人民銀行（中央銀行）が元高抑制姿勢を緩めた。

人民元は一時１ドル＝６．６９５０元と、２３年１月１６日以来の高値を付けた。オフショア人民元はアジア時間で約０．０３％高の１ドル＝６．６９４６元で推移した。

人民銀は取引開始前に対ドル基準値を６．７４８７元と２３年２月３日以来の元高水準に設定した。基準値はほぼ１年にわたり市場予想より元安水準に設定され、人民銀が元の上昇ペースを抑えようとしていると受け止められてきた。しかし今月に入り基準値の元高方向への設定が加速し、人民銀が抑制姿勢を緩めたとの見方が出ている。

ゴールドマン・サックスのアナリストはリポートで、米中首脳会談を控えた時期の基準値の強さは、過去の実績と一致しており、オフショア・スポット相場がさらに上昇する余地が拡大していると指摘。

「首脳会談が開催されるという事実は、安定した貿易関係の維持に寄与するはずだ。中国の政策当局者は持続的かつ緩やかな元高を容認することに引き続き安心感を持つだろう」と述べた。

一方、ＯＣＢＣはノートで、元上昇と相対的な安定は米中交渉にとって建設的な背景を作り、競争的な通貨切り下げとの新たな批判の余地を減らすものの、今回の人民銀の動きを持続的な元高サイクルの始まりと解釈することには慎重であるべきだと指摘した。「米中金利差が大きく、国内のファンダメンタルズが依然として弱い状況を踏まえると、最近の上昇の一部は人民元の根本的な再評価というより、首脳会談に向けた政策主導の安定化を反映している可能性がある」と述べた。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：前途開けた中国人民銀行、「バズーカ砲」不要か コラム：人民元／円相場の記録的高騰に見る円の構造的脆弱性＝植野大作氏 焦点：人民元リスクは上振れ方向、当局が抑制で対応か 焦点：人民元国際化に低金利の追い風、起債や融資が拡大 コラム：人民元高が堅調な中国輸出の妨げとならない理由 最終更新: 9/21(月) 18:43 ロイター

item.title: Wall Street rallies as AI optimism reignites and Treasury yields retreat
item.description: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq surged toward record highs on Monday, lifted by gains in Advanced Micro Devices and other AI heavyweights, while Treasury yields retreated from recent highs and crude prices tumbled to an 11-day low on speculation about a potential breakthrough in Middle East talks at a UN meeting this week.
item.dc:creator: Noel Randewich, Johann Cherian
item.content:encoded: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq surged toward record highs on Monday, lifted by gains in Advanced Micro Devices and other AI heavyweights, while Treasury yields retreated from recent highs and crude prices tumbled to an 11-day low on speculation about a potential breakthrough in Middle East talks at a UN meeting this week. Chip stocks rallied, with Intel (INTC.O) and Arm Holdings surging over 12%, and the PHLX semiconductor index (.SOX) jumping 3.7%. Advanced Micro Devices (AMD.O) rose as much as 10% to reach a market capitalization of $1 trillion for the first time. The stock was last up 8%. The Nasdaq was less than 0.1% below its June 2 record-high close, while the S&P 500 was about 0.5% below its August 13 record-high close. Investors pointed to signs that suggest [USN:L1N45A11J TEXT:"spending"] on AI is [USN:L1N45A0H1 TEXT:"still expanding"], despite recent safety warnings from leaders of AI giants a week ago that triggered a global tech selloff. The benchmark US 10-year yield fell below the psychologically important 5% level as Brent crude futures dipped below $100 a barrel to their lowest level since September 9. While Washington and Tehran exchanged threats through the weekend, US President Donald Trump said he would be [USN:L1N45C06F TEXT:"open to meeting"] Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, who is expected to attend the UN General Assembly in New York this week. "We've been kind of programmed to follow the price of oil and the yield on the US 10-year, and if you look at those two things today, they've shifted from being headwinds to tailwinds for this market, at least in the near term," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth. Meta (META.O) soared 11% after Wells Fargo hiked its price target on the social media platform following the recent launch of its Muse AI assistant. The S&P 500 jumped 1.44% to 7,760.29 points, and it was less than 1% below its August 13 record-high close. The Nasdaq gained 2.13% to 27,086.06 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 0.61% at 51,996.40 points. Seven of the 11 S&P 500 sector indexes rose, led by communication services (.SPLRCL) , up 4.3%, followed by a 2.0% gain in information technology (.SPLRCT) . The S&P 500 last Friday traded at just under 19 times expected earnings, its lowest valuation since 2023, according to LSEG data. AI-related heavyweights are responsible for much of the recent increase in earnings expectations. Investors remained wary of the interest-rate outlook after the US Federal Reserve last week [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"raised rates for the first time in three years"] to fight inflation. Traders see a 50% chance of another hike next month, CME's FedWatch showed. Commentary from at least 10 central bank policymakers is due this week. US-listed shares of companies exposed to Greenland rose following progress in diplomatic negotiations between the [USN:L6N45B02X TEXT:"United States and Denmark"] about the status of Greenland. Greenland Mines (GRML.O) tripled in value, while Greenland Energy (GLND.O) more than doubled. A [USN:L8N45A068 TEXT:"China-US summit"] on Thursday could cover topics including potentially extending the trade truce between the two superpowers, the Iran war and regulation of AI. A report said the US proposed to extend the [USN:FWN45D0BX TEXT:"trade truce"] by six months, while China sought a longer extension. Bitcoin , a key marker of risk tolerance, rose 6% to a more than seven-month high, lifting Coinbase (COIN.O) and Strategy (MSTR.O) more than 4%. Paramount Skydance (PSKY.O) rallied over 4% after a source told Reuters the company had [USN:L4N45D0YQ TEXT:"reached a settlement"] with California and 11 other states suing to block its $110 billion merger with Warner Bros Discovery (WBD.O) . Advancing issues outnumbered falling ones within the S&P 500 (.AD.SPX) by a 1.6-to-one ratio. The S&P 500 posted five new highs and 27 new lows; the Nasdaq recorded 51 new highs and 102 new lows.

item.title: ノボの株価下落、一時7.7％安－業績回復への具体策乏しく失望広がる
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 21日の株式市場でデンマークの製薬会社ノボノルディスクが下落。急成長する肥満症治療薬市場で米イーライリリーに首位の座を奪われる中、マイク・ドゥスター最高経営責任者（CEO）から、より具体的な業績回復策が示されることを期待していた投資家の間で失望が広がった。

同社は今後数年間に5つを超える大型薬を発売し、新たに230億ドル（約3兆6100億円）超の売上高を生み出す方針を示したものの、株価は一時7.7%急落した。

ノルドネットの投資エコノミスト、ペール・ハンセン氏はリポートで、「株価上昇の材料となり得る具体的な新情報が見当たらないため、投資家は株式を売っている」と指摘した。

ノボは、肥満症をより治療しやすい疾患へと変えた新たな治療薬をいち早く投入したにもかかわらず、リリーに後れを取っている。

ドゥスター氏はロンドンで開かれた行事で「われわれはもっと努力する必要があるし、そうする」と述べ、自社の開発パイプライン拡充に加え、企業買収も検討するとした。ただ、何が具体的に成長を押し上げるのかについて、プレゼンテーションでは詳細を欠いた。

ノボはこれまでに、今年の利益と売上高が最大6%減少する可能性があるとしている。

原題：Novo Disappoints Investors Who Sought More Robust Sales Targets

item.title: Merz clings on after German election 'disaster'
item.description: Chancellor Friedrich Merz was clinging to power on Monday after his conservative party tumbled to its worst regional election defeat in postwar Germany and members of his coalition clashed over his unpopular reform agenda.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Rinke, Matthias Williams
item.content:encoded: Chancellor Friedrich Merz was clinging to power on Monday after his conservative party [USN:L1N45C01D TEXT:"tumbled"] to its worst regional election defeat in postwar Germany and members of his coalition clashed over his unpopular [USN:L8N4340M1 TEXT:"reform agenda"]. Merz himself described Sunday's loss in the northeastern state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania as a "disaster" after his Christian Democrats (CDU) missed the minimum threshold to enter the regional parliament. The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) took first place. While it fell well short of a majority, it was the second time it had topped a state election within a month and sees its regional wins as building momentum towards national power. Merz's party also bled votes in a second election in the state of Berlin, which could see the [USN:L1N45C05W TEXT:"far-left Die Linke party"], the descendants of the Communist Party that once ran East Germany, take power in a coalition after winning most seats. GERMAN CHANCELLOR'S FUTURE IN THE BALANCE Sunday's results may not prove a knock-out blow for Merz, but his low approval ratings and the AfD's surge have left his future hanging [USN:L8N4571NP TEXT:"in the balance"]. Several conservative state premiers met on Sunday to take stock after publicly backing Merz in an open letter last week. "The meeting was not about a revolt or a plot against Chancellor Merz," one of the participants of the meeting told Reuters. "However, there was agreement that the chancellor needs to deliver more following the CDU's difficult results in the state elections." On Monday Merz repeated a pledge to press on with his reform agenda, which he says is vital to revive sluggish growth in Europe's largest economy. "... but we know that we also owe it to people to provide answers to their concerns and fears," he added. Merz said there had been no discussion about his position. Sunday's elections have brought tensions with some members of Merz's centre-left Social Democrat (SPD) coalition partners to the surface, with calls to pull back on some aspects of the reform programme, including pensions. "We can't just carry on like this," said SPD co-party leader Baerbel Bas. Germany's economy has been struggling since the pandemic to regain momentum, with competition from China as well as higher energy prices challenging its export-driven economic model. Some business leaders urged Merz to stay the course. "Economic strength is not built by waiting but by actively shaping the future. We cannot afford to lose momentum now," said Jochen Hanebeck, the CEO of chipmaker Infineon (IFXGn.DE) , in a LinkedIn post. BITTER PILL FOR GERMANY'S IMMIGRANTS The AfD party leads in national opinion polls but has been kept from power by the other main parties' refusal to work with it, in a policy known as the "firewall" that has been increasingly scrutinised as the AfD gained strength. Its hardline stance on immigration has left some in Germany of migrant background [USN:L8N44Z0U7 TEXT:"questioning their future"]. "The fact that the AfD is in the lead is quite a bitter pill to swallow," said Yasmin Goudarzi, an educational scientist. In Berlin, Die Linke topped the polls in a state election for the first time on a campaign to nationalise housing from corporate landlords and put a cap on rents, echoing the rise of New York Mayor [USN:L6N42W12S TEXT:"Zohran Mamdani"]. Merz, who was elected last year on a promise to return Germany to growth, has struggled to win over voters, as a stream of communication missteps served to compound resentment over pension, tax and healthcare reforms. Manuela Schwesig, the popular Social Democrat state premier of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, whose success in limiting AfD gains was one of the few positive aspects of the election from the coalition government's perspective, was often strongly critical of the chancellor during the campaign. Schwesig, sometimes seen as a potential next SPD national leader, is likely to remain in power in her state. She said the AfD had won votes by criticising [USN:L1N4500XU TEXT:"Germany's support for Ukraine"], a message that the [USN:L8N45D0Q6 TEXT:"Kremlin also capitalised on"] in comments by its spokesperson on Monday. The AfD wants to restore ties with Moscow and characterises sanctions on Russia as self-sabotaging, by cutting off access to Russia's vast cheap energy resources. Some Germans in Schwerin, the state capital of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, expressed concern about the rise of the far-right AfD in a country still troubled by its Nazi past. "The troublemakers who voted for the AfD clearly weren't paying attention in history class," said Detlef Spelker, a passerby. "We've been in a similar situation before, almost 100 years ago. Inflation, problems with jobs, nobody had any money. We'll see what this brings now." AfD co-leader Alice Weidel on Monday again rejected accusations that her party was the heir to the Nazis, branding Adolf Hitler a "left-wing extremist". She said the AfD had now replaced Merz's CDU as the real home for right-leaning Germans.

item.description: DUBLIN, Sept 21 : The lead EU data privacy regulator for most of the biggest internet companies fined Alphabet's Google €403 million ($463 million) after an inquiry into its processing of location data, policies the search engine said have since been updated.Ireland's Data Protection Commission said on Mond

FAST

DUBLIN, Sept 21 : The lead EU data privacy regulator for most of the biggest internet companies fined Alphabet's Google €403 million ($463 million) after an inquiry into its processing of location data, policies the search engine said have since been updated. Ireland's Data Protection Commission said on Monday it found Google had infringed European Union privacy rules known as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) through three of its specific features – 'Web & App Activity', 'Location History' and 'Location Accuracy' — from 2018 to 2020. A spokesperson for Google said the case centred around historical policies, and that it had launched robust tools and significantly evolved its practices on managing location data since 2019. Google, which is subject to three separate ongoing statutory inquiries that the DPC said were at an advanced stage, was nevertheless ordered by the regulator to bring its location data processing into compliance within six months.

The fine was the fourth largest of the more than €4 billion in total levied by the DPC since it became the lead EU regulator for most big US tech firms under the strict 2018 GDPR due to the location of companies' EU operations in Ireland. "As a result of Google's failures, individuals could have been unaware that their location was being used to, for example, influence them with ads or to infer their interests, and could lose control over their personal data," DPC Deputy Commissioner Graham Doyle said in a statement. The DPC opened the inquiry in 2020 following complaints from several European consumer rights organisations, including the pan-European consumers' organisation BEUC, regarding Google's processing of location data. The infringements included the lawfulness and fairness of Google's processing of location data in 'Web & App Activity', an account setting that processes information related to users’ activity on Google services, and 'Location History', which keeps track of users' location through mobile devices. Google said it has introduced updates since the period investigated that allow users to automatically delete personal data on a rolling basis, store timeline data directly on a device, and manage how data, including location, is used for ads. It also stores an estimated general area rather than a precise device location when a user searches on Google, it added. ($1 = 0.8712 euros)

item.title: Spanish PM Sanchez says AI industry cannot be self-regulated
item.description: Artificial intelligence cannot be self-regulated by those who control the technology, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Artificial intelligence cannot be self-regulated by those who control the technology, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said on Monday. Governments worldwide are racing to set rules for AI as concerns grow over privacy, discrimination, job losses, misinformation and the concentration of computing power among a handful of tech giants. Speaking at an event on AI regulation in Madrid, Sanchez, an outspoken critic of "tech oligarchs", said his government would reinforce its defensive cybersecurity measures to respond to what he described as "aggressive" frontier AI models. He outlined a 12-month roadmap aimed at supporting responsible deployment and economic growth. The plan includes a proposed AI gigafactory as well as new models developed with the Barcelona Supercomputing Centre for climate, health and energy uses. Sanchez said data centres needed to meet high environmental and energy standards while protecting data autonomy and benefiting local communities. "We must develop this technology not behind citizens' backs ... but in a way that people see it as an opportunity rather than a tool for depleting their scarce resources," he added. Sanchez's remarks came days after the heads of leading U.S. AI labs [USN:L4N456128 TEXT:"called"] for a slowdown in the technology's development, [USN:L4N45616J TEXT:"warning"] it could soon improve on its own and slip beyond human control.

item.title: 中国、習近平国家主席の訪米を正式発表－首脳会談で通商やAI巡り協議
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 中国政府は21日、習近平国家主席がトランプ米大統領と会談するため、米国を訪問すると正式に発表した。米中の貿易戦争を巡る1年間の「休戦」措置が、期限を迎えつつある中での訪米となる。

中国外務省は今年5月、トランプ氏の招待を受け、習氏が秋に米国を公式訪問する予定だと説明していた。

中国外務省の郭嘉昆報道官によると、習氏は23－25日に国賓として米国を訪問する。郭氏は21日、北京での定例記者会見で、両国が「相違を適切に管理」するため共同で取り組む中で、習氏はトランプ氏と「二国間関係や世界の平和と発展に関わる重要な問題について踏み込んだ意見交換」を行うと説明した。

郭氏は「半年の間に両首脳が相互訪問することは、歴史的意義を持つ節目となる」とも強調した。トランプ氏と習氏は5月に北京で会談している。

習氏の訪米は、2023年にサンフランシスコでのアジア太平洋経済協力会議（APEC）首脳会議への出席と併せ、バイデン前米大統領と会談して以来となる。米中が昨年、韓国で取り決めた貿易戦争の休戦措置が延長されるとの観測は強まりつつあり、両国は米国産エネルギーや農産物などの製品への関税引き下げについて協議している。

首脳会談を前に、米中当局者は20日、ニューヨークでAIや貿易、投資を巡り協議した。ベッセント米財務長官は会談を「非常に成功した」と評価し、AIに関する対話の枠組みを設けることで両国が合意したと述べた。

トランプ氏は、習氏のために国賓晩餐会を開くとしており、アップルのティム・クック会長とオープンAIのサム・アルトマン最高経営責任者（CEO）が出席する見通しだ。

首脳会談では、イラン戦争やレアアースの供給、AIを巡る競争も議題となる可能性が高い。中国はイラン産原油の最大の買い手で、米国によるイランへの経済的締め付けの取り組みに対し、協力を急いでいないもようだ。

中国政府は、台湾の地位が数少ない譲れない一線の一つであることを、米国側に改めて伝える可能性が高い。米国は、中国が自国領とみなす台湾の最大の軍事・政治的支援国となっている。

item.title: ＶＷ・ポルシェ株続落、減損含む業績悪化警告で 追加人員削減報道も
item.description: ［フランクフルト ２１日 ロイター］ - 欧州自動車最大手のフォルクスワーゲン（ＶＷ）株が２１日序盤の取引で前週末に続...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＶＷ・ポルシェ株続落、減損含む業績悪化警告で　追加人員削減報道も 9/21 17:37 配信

資料写真：2025年5月14日、ドイツのドレスデンで行われたメディアツアー中、ドイツの自動車メーカー、フォルクスワーゲンの電気自動車「ID.3」の最終検査ラインにVWのロゴが見える。 REUTERS/Matthias Rietschel/File Photo

［フランクフルト　２１日　ロイター］ - 欧州自動車最大手のフォルクスワーゲン（ＶＷ）株が２１日序盤の取引で前週末に続き下落。高級スポーツカー部門ポルシェでの６０億ユーロ（６８億８０００万ドル）ののれん代減損を含む業績予想下方修正を嫌気した。

０７１３ＧＭＴ（日本時間午後４時１３分）時点で、ＶＷ株は２％安。ポルシェ株も２．８％下落した。１８日に同じく見通しを下方修正したＶＷの筆頭株主ポルシェＳＥも３．５％安となっている。

ＶＷは１８日、中国市場の低迷や退職引当金の増加、ポルシェの深刻な状況を理由に、２０２６年の利益率見通しを従来の４─５．５％から最大１％に引き下げた。

大きく依存していた中国、米国両市場の急激な変化が圧迫。中国市場で２４年に首位の座を失った。

アーノ・アントリッツ最高財務責任者（ＣＦＯ）はロイターが確認した社内メモで、世界最大の自動車市場である中国市場が２０％縮小していること、アジア勢が欧州市場で攻勢を強めていること、利益率の低い電気自動車（ＥＶ）の販売が増えていることに言及し、「時間を失う余裕はない」と述べた。

さらに１９日、ＶＷの大規模再建計画には、ポルシェでさらに４０００人超削減する案が含まれていると独経済紙ハンデルスブラットが報じた。

ハンデルスブラットによると、ＶＷ監査役会が最近合意した、独自動車グループとして過去最大規模の再編に関する文書では、ポルシェで「約４１００人」の人員削減を提案している。約７億ユーロ（８億３８０万ドル）の間接費不足の解消を目指すという。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：エネルギー高・金利高の二重苦、世界の株価を圧迫へ コラム：円急伸で揺らぐキャリートレード、見つからない次の調達通貨 アングル：世界市場が当面向き合う6つのリスク、地政学や金融政策・ＡＩなど 焦点：米国株の強さ再び、「ＴＩＡＲＡ」取引衰え「ＴＩＮＡ」取引が復活 アングル：中東緊迫で市場は2022年の教訓参照　ロシアのウクライナ侵攻時の動き再検証 最終更新: 9/21(月) 17:37 ロイター

item.title: 習主席の訪米発表、重要問題でトランプ氏と意見交換と中国外務省
item.description: ［北京 ２１日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［北京　２１日　ロイター］ - 中国外務省は２１日の声明で、習近平国家主席がトランプ米大統領の招待により２３─２５日に米国を公式訪問すると発表した。

発表後の定例記者会見で、郭嘉昆報道官は、習氏が訪問中に「中米関係や世界の平和と発展に関する重要問題について、トランプ氏と踏み込んだ意見交換を行う」と述べた。

両国首脳が６カ月以内に相互訪問することは「歴史的かつ画期的な意義がある」とし、「中国は米国と協力し、対話と協力を強化し、相違を適切に管理した上で、両国民の幸福を絶えず向上させ、世界の平和と安定、繁栄を促進する用意がある」と述べた。

MILAN, Sept 21 : Central banks need to understand who benefits from artificial intelligence-driven gains, as their distribution will help shape aggregate demand and inflation, European Central Bank Governing Council member Fabio Panetta said on Monday. • AI is set to transform productivity and growth, labour and financial markets, and payment systems, Panetta said. • If AI mainly creates new tasks and raises expected labour income, demand could increase before AI's full productivity benefits materialise, prolonging inflationary pressures, he added. • Panetta, who is also governor of the Bank of Italy, was speaking at an event hosted by the National Bank of Ukraine.
